title: feat: use paired function items for hosted agents
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Replace managed `mcp_call` output/history with paired `function_call` / `function_call_output` items: separate item IDs, shared call IDs, namespaced tools and JSON-string results. Tool failures use MCP `isError`; no legacy managed-history mode.
- Render completed server tools through the shared Chat adapter without client re-execution. Text still streams; pending client tool arguments wait until the terminal response. Native provider MCP items remain supported.
- Validate complete stateless pairs with shared Zod schemas; preserve required usage, billing, cache controls and media rendering. Net production-code change: +137 lines.
- Verified 211 focused tests, Gen TypeScript and Biome checks, including OpenAI SDK stream consumption, replay, errors and billing failures. LibreChat browser testing remains pending: Docker-free installation needs more than the available 2 GB disk.
- Follows #14516 and the hosted-agent serialization precedent in [LibreChat](https://github.com/danny-avila/LibreChat/blob/b5c5624f138423d072acafe4c91d618a88b16554/packages/api/src/agents/responses/handlers.ts#L206-L235) and [LobeHub](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/5bf3a37e378deb81a83e9f7a63a2441b03368125/packages/openapi/src/services/responses.service.ts#L690-L725). This is protocol alignment, not a claim that every client already renders tool cards.

gist.headline: Tools travel in pairs
gist.blurb: Hosted agents now pack each tool call with its matching result, like two labeled jars of honey on the same shelf. Clients get a cleaner, replayable conversation trail without being asked to run server tools again.
gist.summary: Hosted agents now emit stateless paired `function_call` and `function_call_output` items with separate item IDs, shared call IDs, namespaced tool names, and JSON-string results, replacing legacy managed `mcp_call` history while retaining native provider MCP items.
gist.impact: OpenAI-compatible clients can replay completed server-tool work through the shared Chat adapter without client re-execution, while text continues streaming and client-tool arguments wait for the terminal response.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy garden workbench where Polli is carefully pairing two matching, tagged API scrolls: a `function_call` scroll and a `function_call_output` scroll joined by a shared pollen-colored thread. A cheerful CRT Monitor Robot watches the completed tool cards appear on its screen, while code-plants and small flowers make the protocol work feel like orderly garden tending rather than mysterious machinery.
